taxonomic_note: Current Kew accepts one species in Taxodium with three varieties; Central Texas baldcypress is represented at species level here, with var. distichum as the likely local infraspecific concept.
look_here_first: Start with the deciduous feathery branchlets and buttressed wet-site trunk. Baldcypress is a large deciduous conifer with flat two-ranked leaves on many lateral shoots, fibrous reddish-brown bark, round woody cones, and often knees or a swollen fluted base near water.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays and Travis natural riparian-community documentation plus Williamson County occurrence/listing.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Species-level learner; no forced local variety assignment.

best_field_traits: feathery two-ranked leaves on many lateral shoots
foliage turns coppery and sheds in winter
swollen/fluted trunk base in wet sites
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Deciduous conifer + feathery two-ranked foliage + wet-site buttressed trunk/knees + round cones is the core field package.
